name: Bain de Soleil

lead: Bain de Soleil was a tanning-oriented sun care brand, famous for an orange gel launched in Paris in 1925.

paras: It was positioned as a tanning aid with low SPF rather than a high-protection sunscreen.
No brand-specific studies were found. Low-SPF products give correspondingly lower sunburn protection.

lead: Bain de Soleil ('sun bath' in French) was a tanning and sun care brand best known for an orange gel and low-SPF products. Wikipedia dates its origin to 1925, when Paris hairdresser Monsieur Antoine developed an orange gel tanning formula; Lanvin later introduced it in the U.S. [1]. Bayer discontinued the brand in December 2019 [1].

A reference text from the AI-generated Grokipedia, which may contain errors, adds that a 2024 deal was announced for a relaunch; this is unverified here [2]. No clinical studies of the brand are known.

paras: Per Wikipedia, the product originated as an orange gel in Paris in 1925 and reached the U.S. through Lanvin [1]. Procter & Gamble sold the brand to Pfizer in 1995, with production moving to Parsippany, New Jersey and the line expanding to sunless and after-sun products; Pfizer sold it to Schering-Plough on 7 October 1999 [1]. Bayer is listed as owner at discontinuation in December 2019 [1].

Grokipedia reports that the brand's low-SPF positioning fell out of step with demand for higher protection, that fans petitioned and resold vintage tubes, and that a company announced plans in November 2024 to acquire and relaunch it; these details come from an AI-generated source and are unconfirmed [2].
The brand is associated with tanning-aid products rather than high-protection sunscreens [1][2].

No studies found. Related laboratory work includes a 1981 hairless-mouse study comparing seven sunscreens' protective factors against UVB effects on epidermal DNA synthesis; whether this brand was among them is not established here [3].
